-Tunneled HD line placement (___):

# Acute on chronic kidney disease: Etiology for his worsening 
kidney function thought to be overdiuresis after last admission 
for diastolic CHF exacerbation.

He appeared dry on exam with flat neck 
veins and poor skin turgor, weight was 6kg down from his most 
recent discharge.

His BUN/Cr did not initially improve with 
holding diuresis and the renal tram was consulted.

The decision 
was made to proceed with a trial of dialysis given that his 
severe itching appeared to be related to his uremia.

He 
received tunneled line on ___ and had first session of HD
___, which he tolerated well but became slightly hypothermic.
He received a total of 3 HD sessions during this admission.

He 
was started on nephrocaps and sevelamer was increased from 800mg 
tid to ___ tid.
HepB sAg and HepB sAb were both negative,
HepC was negative.
PPD was placed ___ and was negative on

He will continue to receive HD at ___ in ___ 
on a MWF schedule after discharge.

# Hypothermia: Became hypothermic to ___ during first HD 
session.

BCx were drawn which are NGTD at discharge and UCx 
also had no growth.
CXR showed no evidence of infection.

His 
temperature improved after the first session and he had no 
futher episodes of hypothermia.

# Chronic diastolic CHF (EF >55%): As mentioned above, he 
appeared volume depleted on exam, neck veins were flat, no 
edema, and skin turgor was poor.

We held his torsemide and 
metolazone.

He was continued on metoprolol and his volume will 
be regulated with dialysis in the future.

His weight increased 
from 119kg to 122.2kg at the time of discharge and he appeared 
euvoluemic at discharge.

# LLE cellulitis: Had warmth and erythema of the LLE, cellulits 
was likely likely related to his uremia and repeated itching.

He was started on Keflex for 7 days, which he completed in the 
hospital and will not need further antibiotics at discharge.

He 
remained afebrile, WBC not elevated and BCx were negative.

The 
warmth and erythema had improved at the time of discharge.

# H/o DVT/PE - He has a h/o PE which occurred many years ago (pt 
not sure when, but ___ years ago).
It is also unclear how many
PEs he had and in what setting.

Warfarin was held for 4 days and he 
received 2mg Vitamin K during this admission for tunneled line 
placement.

The indication for lifelong anticoagulation was not 
clear given that we are unsure how many PEs he has had in the 
past.
He will have his INR checked on ___.

Of 
note, his mixing study which was sent during prior admission 
showed the presence of an inhibitor, which explains his elevated
PTT.
--Chronic issues--
# COPD/Obesity Hypoventilation/OSA/Sleep Disordered Breathing:

The patient has a history of hypercarbic respiratory failure due 
to sleep-disordered breathing and likely obesity hypoventilation 
syndrome.

Noted to be 
exquisitely sensitive to diuresis, often causing metabolic 
alkalosis induced with volume contraction, decreasing 
respiratory drive.

Wears 2L NC at baseline, which was continued 
this admission.

He was also contnued on CPAP at night and his 
home COPD medications: albuterol, Spiriva, fluticasone
# CAD - No chest pain or pressure this admission.

He was 
continued on ASA 81mg daily.
# Anemia: Hematocrit remained at his baseline.
# NIDDM: Blood sugar remained well controlled.

He was covered 
with a Humalog sliding scale during this admission
# Rheumatoid arthritis: He was continued on Plaquenil

# Depression/Bipolar Disorder/Schizoaffective disorder: Stable,

oxcarbazepine.

continued on metoprolol.
